title: Fourth in the Queue
statement: Consider all composite positive integers that have no prime factor less than $20$. When these integers are listed in increasing order, what is the fourth integer in the list?
hints: Write down the primes greater than $20$, starting with the smallest. Every prime factor of a number in the list must come from these primes.

Use prime factorisation: a composite number is a product of at least two primes, counted with repetition. So each number in the list is a product of at least two primes from $23, 29, 31, 37, \dots$, and the smallest numbers will be products of exactly two of them.

The three products $23 \cdot 23$, $23 \cdot 29$ and $23 \cdot 31$ are in the list. To find the next number, don't assume that it is another multiple of $23$. Compare the next product that uses $23$ with the smallest product that doesn't use $23$.
solution: Every composite positive integer can be written as a product of at least two primes, where a prime may be repeated. The primes above $20$ are $23, 29, 31, 37, \dots$, because the other numbers from $21$ to $36$ are even or are one of $21 = 3 \cdot 7$, $25 = 5^2$, $27 = 3^3$, $33 = 3 \cdot 11$ and $35 = 5 \cdot 7$. So a number is in the list exactly when it is a product of at least two primes from $23, 29, 31, 37, \dots$. The number $29^2 = 841$ is in the list. We now find every number in the list below $841$. Let $n < 841$ be such a number and let $p$ be its smallest prime factor. Write $n = p \cdot k$. Since $n$ is composite, $k > 1$, and every prime factor of $k$ is at least $p$, so $k \ge p$ and $n \ge p^2$. If $p \ge 29$, then $n \ge 841$, which is false. Hence $p = 23$ and $n = 23k$. Since $23 \cdot 36 = 828$ and $23 \cdot 37 = 851$, the condition $23k < 841$ means that $k \le 36$. Also, every prime factor of $k$ is at least $23$. If $k$ were composite, it would be a product of at least two such primes, so $k \ge 23^2 = 529$, which contradicts $k \le 36$. So $k$ is prime with $23 \le k \le 36$, which leaves $k = 23$, $29$ or $31$. These values give $23 \cdot 23 = 529$, $23 \cdot 29 = 667$ and $23 \cdot 31 = 713$, each of which is in the list. So exactly three numbers in the list are below $841$, and the list begins $529, 667, 713, 841$. The tempting next multiple of $23$, namely $23 \cdot 37 = 851$, comes too late. The answer is $841$. Why this works. prime-factorization, bounding: factorisation reduces the list to products of large primes, and the bound $n \ge p^2$ shows which of those products can come before $29^2$.
